In the dead of night, Chancellor Rosenthal of Germany flies out from Berlin. His message was sent to Jim webb, the new American president, and the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom had both been replied to in the affirmative. They will be meeting in the White House of all places. He’s palms are sweaty, his heart pounding. He’s never done something like this, but his whole term in office has been spent fighting with the DNVP and parties they’ve rallied to their cause. Even the Greens have been drifting in their direction

He knows that the US/UK did bully Merkel. Steiner was right about that. It kills him a little inside, to grovel to foreign nations for help to run the nation he was elected to run. But desperate times call for desperate measures. If Steiner wasn’t stopped, he was sure to become the Chancellor of Germany. That men was blessed with the Devil’s own charisma. This was unacceptable. The world would declare war on Germany for making the wrong choice.

And Rosenthal had to put an end to that.

He couldn’t trust his own government members. Time had shown that DNVP has sympathizers everywhere. Just last night he’d read an article in the paper about how a great majority of policemen in Berlin were more than likely to be DNVP members, including the police chief himself. And this was to say nothing of the DNVP, with the combination of the AfD, now had the support of the majority of the army. That was an open secret! If he talked about this at all with his staff, surely one of them would report it to Steiner.

He was a Jew, and Steiner was a Nazi. Rosenthal had every reason to fear. How many people looked at him each day, smiled, side nice things, worked for him, yet secretly wished to see him sent to a gas chamber? His grandfather had survived the gas chambers himself, but Steiner knew Rosenthal. Steiner did not like Rosenthal. Steiner would surely kill Rosenthal.

His streams of thoughts only came to a halt countless hours later. It was only when he stood in a clandestine room with the most powerful man in the world, newly elected Jim Webb, and the leader of the United Kingdom, that for the first time in a long while, Rosenthal felt himself calming down.

“Are we secure?” Rosenthal asked, not willing to yet take a seat. “I do not wish for a repeat of what happened with Merkel.”

Webb nodded.

Rosenthal let out a very, very long breath he’d only been partially aware he’d been keeping.

“Gentlemen,” he said, wiping sweat of his forehead. “Germany is dying. A cancer wracks us and will never go away, perhaps not even if excised with a knife. But with your expert surgeons, we at least stand of a chance of stemming it before it metastasizes.”

He looked both men in the eye, long and hard.

“And that cancer’s name is Gustav Steiner.”
